adoption.rationale: The exact pinned constant documents the JavaScript ASCII word set and adds dot and hyphen; the shared segment tester applies it to all three exported helpers, and INVARIANTS.md declares the same partition. This is only a library validation invariant. The Real-Router GO decision is scale-based; no untrusted remote input or security impact is claimed.

contract.declared_domain: Non-empty ASCII segment strings of at most 10,000 JavaScript UTF-16 code units passed to startsWithSegment, endsWithSegment, or includesSegment. The formal proof is a length-independent one-code-unit alphabet query. The exact-source Node gate additionally checks all ASCII strings of length one and two, deterministic mixed strings, Unicode/control examples, and the 10,000/10,001 length boundary.
contract.guarantee: For each of the three pinned route segment tester helpers, a non-empty ASCII segment accepted by SAFE_SEGMENT_PATTERN contains only ASCII letters, digits, underscore, dot, or hyphen. The helper checks the 10,000-code-unit maximum separately; this contract does not assert route matching, authorization, or security impact.
contract.input_source: The segment string passed by an application caller to the exported route-utils startsWithSegment, endsWithSegment, or includesSegment helpers. The reviewed repository documents and implements this as route-segment configuration/API input; no remote attacker source is established here.

attempts.domain: For an ASCII code unit, membership in the exact pinned segment regex implies that the code unit is an ASCII letter, digit, underscore, dot, or hyphen
